messages.subject: How to embolden math expressions
parts:
Hello Community

 

I wish to embolden an annotated math expression. The ‘ggplot2’ code is below.

 

wtPlot1 <- ggplot(wtData, aes(x=Week, y=Weight, color=Group)) + geom_point(size=3.5) + theme (panel.background=element_rect("white")) + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) + theme(panel.border = element_rect(color="black", fill=NA, size=1.5)) + scale_color_manual(values=c("red", "blue")) + geom_smooth(method="lm", aes(fill=Group), alpha=0.1) + labs(x="Week ", y="Weight (lb)", color="Group") + theme(axis.title.y=element_text(size=16, face="bold")) + theme(axis.title.x=element_text(size=16, face="bold")) + annotate("text", x=3.5, y=269, size=6, family="serif", fontface="bold", label="Control") + annotate("text", x=3.5, y=268, parse=TRUE, size=6, label="y==-0.19*'x' +276.5") + annotate("text", x=3.5, y=267, parse=TRUE, size=6, label="R^2==0.29")

For example, the mathematical expressions "y==-0.19*'x' +276.5" and "R^2==0.29" will be more visible on the graph if they are bold. The statement ‘face="bold"’ has no effect on these mathematical expressions.  Is there some other statement that will embolden math expressions?

Thanks

James Henson
